artiest/bon-jovi.text:
Bon Jovi was formed in 1983 in Sayreville, New Jersey, around the singer Jon Bon Jovi. The best-known line-up also included guitarist Richie Sambora, keyboard player David Bryan, drummer Tico Torres and bassist Alec John Such. Bon Jovi joined hard rock to pop: distorted guitars, but choruses that a whole stadium can sing along to. The band is one of the best-known examples of 1980s glam metal and stadium rock, when MTV demanded an image from rock bands as well as a sound.

The song Runaway appeared in 1983 on a compilation album from the radio station WAPP, and the debut album Bon Jovi was released in January 1984. For Slippery When Wet (1986) the band brought in the professional songwriter Desmond Child. The album, produced by Bruce Fairbairn, spent eight weeks at number 1 on the Billboard 200. You Give Love a Bad Name and Livin' on a Prayer both reached number 1 on the Hot 100. Livin' on a Prayer tells the story of Tommy and Gina, a working-class couple trying to keep their heads above water.

New Jersey (1988) produced five top 10 singles, a record for a hard rock album. In 2000 the band reached a new, younger audience with It's My Life. Bon Jovi has sold more than 130 million records worldwide. In 2018 the group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/bon-jovi.listen: Livin' on a Prayer (1986): the talking guitar riff is played by Richie Sambora through a talk box, a small tube with which he shapes the guitar sound with his mouth. In the last chorus, listen for the jump up of three semitones, from E minor to G minor.

artiest/bon-scott.text:
Bon Scott was an Australian singer and lyricist, the second lead singer of the hard rock band AC/DC from 1974 until his death in 1980. He was born Ronald Belford Scott on 9 July 1946 in Forfar, Scotland, and grew up in Kirriemuir, where his parents ran a bakery. In 1952 the family emigrated to Australia. He got his nickname Bon at school: there was another Ronald in the class, and his classmates played on the words Bonnie Scotland. In Fremantle he learned to drum in a bagpipe band. He left school at fifteen and worked as a farm labourer and a lobster fisherman, among other jobs.

In 1964 he formed his first band, the Spektors, in which he drummed and sometimes sang. He then played in the Valentines and Fraternity, before succeeding AC/DC's original singer, Dave Evans, in 1974. With AC/DC he made seven albums, from High Voltage in 1975 to Dirty Deeds Done Dirt Cheap in 1976, Let There Be Rock in 1977, Powerage in 1978 and Highway to Hell in 1979. The band became popular first in Australia and then internationally. Highway to Hell reached the top twenty in the United States and was the breakthrough.

On 19 February 1980 Scott died after a night out in London. AC/DC considered stopping, but took on Brian Johnson, the singer of the glam rock band Geordie. The next album, Back in Black, came out five months later and was a tribute to Scott. He is often named as one of the greatest frontmen of all time, and his raw voice and brash, humorous lyrics defined the band's sound.
artiest/bon-scott.listen: Listen to Highway to Hell from 1979 and pay attention to his voice: rough, sharp and yet melodic. Hear how the guitar riff and his singing complement each other.

artiest/bono.text:
Bono, the nickname of Paul David Hewson, is an Irish singer, songwriter and activist. He was born in Dublin on 10 May 1960 and grew up in a house on Cedarwood Road, between Finglas and Ballymun. His mother was Anglican and his father Catholic, and he received a mixed Christian upbringing. At Mount Temple Comprehensive School he formed, in 1976 and with school friends, the band that would become U2. His relationship with his future wife, Alison Stewart, also began there. He is U2's lead singer and main lyricist.

Bono is known for his passionate singing and his grand style of writing and performing. His lyrics often contain social and political themes and religious imagery, inspired by his Christian faith. In the early years he gave U2 a rebellious and spiritual tone; later he wrote more from the personal experiences of the band members. With U2 he won twenty-two Grammy Awards and a place in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Outside the band he wrote songs with The Edge for Roy Orbison and Tina Turner, and the music for the musical Spider-Man: Turn Off the Dark and for a London adaptation of A Clockwork Orange.

Bono is also active in the cause of social justice, above all in the fight against extreme poverty and HIV and AIDS in Africa. To that end he co-founded DATA, EDUN, the ONE Campaign and Product Red, and he spoke with politicians and heads of state. In 2005 he was one of Time's Persons of the Year. He has also been criticised, among other things because African companies were left out of the picture and because of tax avoidance in his private finances. He showed how a rock singer can use his fame for a political cause.
artiest/bono.listen: Listen to a U2 song and focus on Bono's voice. Notice how it moves from soft and intimate to loud and pleading, and what that does to the lyrics.

artiest/bonobo.text:
Bonobo is the artist alias of Simon Green, an English musician, producer and DJ who was born in 1976 and now lives in Los Angeles. He made his debut in 1999 on a compilation from the label Tru Thoughts and took his name from the great ape. Bigger labels made offers, but he stayed with Tru Thoughts, where his first album, Animal Magic, was released in 2000. It received mixed reviews but built up a cult following. In 2001 he signed to Ninja Tune, the label of Coldcut.

Dial 'M' for Monkey followed in 2003 and Days to Come in 2006, on which singers such as Bajka provided an organic sound. Black Sands, from 2010, showed that he had grown from samples to real instruments. According to one review, the track Kiara combines eastern strings with chopped-up beats. Later came The North Borders in 2013, Migration in 2017 and Fragments in 2022.

Bonobo began with a trip-hop sound and later also explored jazz and world music. His electronic sound makes much use of live instruments and is recreated on stage by a full band. That places him among the producers who made electronic music sound warm and handmade, on the borderland of downtempo, jazz and world music.
artiest/bonobo.listen: Listen to Kiara. Notice how the strings give an eastern tint to a rhythm of cut-up beats, with a soft bass underneath.

artiest/booker-t-en-the-mg-s.text:
Booker T. & the MG's was an American instrumental R&B and jazz band formed in Memphis, Tennessee, in 1962. The original line-up consisted of Booker T. Jones on organ and piano, Steve Cropper on guitar, Lewie Steinberg on bass and Al Jackson Jr. on drums. In 1965 Donald Duck Dunn took over on bass. As the house band of the Stax label, they played on hundreds of recordings by artists such as Wilson Pickett, Otis Redding, Sam & Dave, Carla Thomas and Albert King. In doing so they helped to shape the typical Stax sound, Memphis soul.

Green Onions came about in the summer of 1962. During a break in the studio, while they were accompanying Billy Lee Riley, the four of them played around with a bluesy organ riff. Stax boss Jim Stewart heard it and recorded it. The track was released with Behave Yourself as the other side, but the DJs and Cropper felt it should be the other way round. It reached number 1 on the American R&B chart and number 3 on the pop chart. Later albums included Soul Dressing, Hip Hug-Her, McLemore Avenue and Melting Pot.

The band consisted of two white and two black members, which made it one of the first racially mixed rock groups, in a time and a city where soul was seen mainly as black culture. Al Jackson was murdered in 1975; Dunn, Cropper and Jones often played together after that. In 1992 the band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/booker-t-en-the-mg-s.listen: Listen to Green Onions. Notice the organ playing the theme, Cropper's short, dry guitar chords and Jackson's tight drumming underneath.

artiest/booker-t-jones.text:
Booker T. Jones was born on 12 November 1944 in Memphis, Tennessee. He was a child prodigy: at school he played oboe, saxophone, trombone, double bass and piano, and in church the organ. At sixteen he played baritone saxophone on Cause I Love You by Carla and Rufus Thomas, the first hit for the label that would later be called Stax.

In the label's record shop he met the guitarist Steve Cropper. In 1962, together with bassist Lewie Steinberg, later replaced by Donald Duck Dunn, and drummer Al Jackson Jr., they formed the band Booker T. & the M.G.'s. Jones played organ. While still at secondary school he co-wrote the instrumental Green Onions, which became a big hit in 1962. Jones then studied classical composition at Indiana University, played with the M.G.'s in Memphis at weekends and worked as a session musician for other Stax artists. With William Bell he wrote Born Under a Bad Sign for Albert King, later made famous by Cream.

He also wrote songs for Eddie Floyd and Otis Redding. In this way Jones stood, as player, writer and arranger, at the centre of the soul that came out of Memphis in those years. In 1970 Jones moved to California and stopped his session work for Stax. Later he made solo albums such as Potato Hole (2009). He received a Grammy for his lifetime achievement. Since the death of Steve Cropper in December 2025 he has been the last surviving original member of the group.
artiest/booker-t-jones.listen: Listen to Green Onions (1962). Notice Jones's short, constantly repeated organ figure above a simple blues progression, and the sharp guitar stabs from Steve Cropper that keep cutting in between.

artiest/bootsy-collins.text:
William Earl Collins, known as Bootsy, is an American bass guitarist, singer and songwriter from Cincinnati, born in 1951. His mother gave him the nickname. In 1968 he formed the band The Pacemakers with his older brother Phelps, known as Catfish. When James Brown's band walked out in March 1970 after a row over money, the brothers and their group became his new backing band: the J.B.'s. They played for Brown for only eleven months, but on some of his fiercest funk records, such as Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine, Super Bad and Soul Power.

Collins then joined George Clinton's collective Parliament-Funkadelic. In 1976 he started Bootsy's Rubber Band, with his brother and the horn section The Horny Horns, among others. The album Bootsy? Player of the Year, from 1978, produced the single Bootzilla. Like Clinton, he played characters, such as Casper the Funky Ghost and Bootzilla, a glittering pop monster from space. He played a star-shaped bass guitar, the Space Bass.

Collins's sound revolves around driving, rhythmic bass lines and funny, crazy vocals. Later he worked with the producer Bill Laswell, with Herbie Hancock and with Deee-Lite, for whom he sang backing vocals on Groove Is in the Heart. Fatboy Slim also brought him in. In 1997 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Parliament-Funkadelic. His hard, rhythmic bass playing had a great influence on funk, soul and even metal.
artiest/bootsy-collins.listen: Listen to Get Up (I Feel Like Being a) Sex Machine by James Brown. Follow only Collins's bass: the song stays on virtually one chord, so all the movement comes from the rhythm of his short, constantly recurring figures.

artiest/boris-berman.text:
Boris Berman is a Russian pianist and teacher, born in Moscow on 3 April 1948. He studied with Lev Oborin at the Moscow Conservatory and made his debut in 1965. He played harpsichord in the only early music ensemble that Russia had at the time, and at the same time worked with contemporary composers such as Alfred Schnittke and Edison Denisov. In Russia he was the first to play works by Arnold Schönberg, Karlheinz Stockhausen, Luciano Berio and György Ligeti. In 1973 he was allowed to leave the Soviet Union for Israel, and in 1979 he left for the United States. There he taught at Boston University, Brandeis University and Indiana University, and he is head of the piano department at the Yale School of Music.

He has played with many soloists and ensembles, including Mischa Maisky, Shlomo Mintz, the Tokyo Quartet, the Vermeer Quartet, the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra and the Gewandhaus Orchestra. His recordings have appeared on Philips, Deutsche Grammophon and Chandos, among others. He was the first pianist to record all of Sergei Prokofiev's solo piano music, in nine CDs on Chandos, with sonatas, concertos and shorter pieces. He also made recordings of Scriabin, Shostakovich, Debussy, Stravinsky and Schnittke, and two records of music for prepared piano by John Cage, which BBC Music Magazine named best recording. His recording of piano quintets by Shostakovich and Schnittke with the Vermeer Quartet was nominated for a Grammy.

Berman is also a juror at competitions in Leeds, Dublin, Shanghai and Tel Aviv and gives masterclasses all over the world. In this way he brought twentieth-century music from the Soviet Union to the West, and trained new pianists.
artiest/boris-berman.listen: Listen to one of Prokofiev's piano sonatas in Berman's recording and notice the sharp, rhythmic passages. Hear how he alternates them with calm, songlike sections.

artiest/boris-vian.text:
Boris Vian was a French polymath, remembered above all as a novelist, born on 10 March 1920 in Ville d'Avray near Paris and died on 23 June 1959. His mother, an amateur pianist and harpist, chose his first name after a performance of the opera Boris Godunov. At the age of twelve he contracted rheumatic fever, after which his parents overprotected him. In 1936 he became interested in jazz; the following year he began to play the trumpet and became a member of the Hot Club de France. In 1939 he helped to organise Duke Ellington's second concert in France.

His novels under his own name have an idiosyncratic style with invented words, wordplay and surreal plots. The best known is L'Écume des jours, published in English as Froth on the Daydream. Under the pseudonym Vernon Sullivan he wrote bizarre parodies of crime fiction, which caused a great stir at the time.

Vian was important for French jazz. In Paris he was the contact for Hoagy Carmichael, Duke Ellington and Miles Davis, wrote for jazz magazines such as Le Jazz Hot and Paris Jazz, and published many articles about jazz in France and the United States. His own songs were also popular in his lifetime, above all the anti-war song Le Déserteur. Others later sang his lyrics, such as Serge Reggiani and Magali Noël on their own albums. Vian shows how literature, jazz and chanson ran together in post-war Paris.
artiest/boris-vian.listen: Listen to Le Déserteur and pay attention to the lyrics, which are written in the form of a letter to the president. Notice how simple the melody is, and what that means for the words.

artiest/borodin-quartet.text:
The Borodin Quartet is a string quartet founded in the Soviet Union in 1944 and is one of the longest-lived quartets in the world. In 2015 it celebrated its seventieth season. The group began as the Moscow Conservatory Quartet, with Mstislav Rostropovich on cello, Rostislav Dubinsky and Vladimir Rabei on violin and Yuri Nikolayevsky on viola, students of Professor Mikhail Terian. Rostropovich withdrew after a few weeks in favour of Valentin Berlinsky, and Nina Barshai and Rudolf Barshai took the places of two others. In 1955 the quartet was named after Alexander Borodin, one of the founders of Russian chamber music.

In 1946 the quartet met Dmitri Shostakovich and became a regular interpreter of his music. Shostakovich consulted the members personally about each of his string quartets, and the quartet played all fifteen of them around the world. It also often played with the pianist Sviatoslav Richter. During the Cold War it was one of the best-known Soviet quartets in the West, thanks to recordings and concerts in the United States and Europe. It played at the funerals of Stalin and Prokofiev, who died on the same day in 1953. Recordings appeared on Melodiya, Teldec, Virgin and Chandos, including all the quartets of Shostakovich and Beethoven.

The 1970s brought a difficult period: Dubinsky defected to the West and the second violinist stopped for health reasons. Berlinsky kept the group out of sight for two years in order to rebuild its own sound. That sound had an almost symphonic volume and a highly developed phrasing that nevertheless kept the group together. All the members were graduates of the Moscow Conservatory.
artiest/borodin-quartet.listen: Listen to a Shostakovich string quartet played by the Borodin Quartet, such as the Quartet no. 8, and notice the full sound of four instruments. Try to hear how they phrase together without any one of them dominating.

artiest/boston-pops-orchestra.text:
The Boston Pops is an American orchestra from Boston that specialises in light classical and popular music. It was founded in 1885 as an offshoot of the Boston Symphony Orchestra and consists mainly of musicians from that orchestra, although usually not all the principal players take part. Its founder, Henry Lee Higginson, wanted to offer concerts of a lighter kind of music in Boston. The first concert was on 11 July 1885 under Adolf Neuendorff. Until 1900 the performances were called Promenade Concerts.

Before 1930 the orchestra had seventeen conductors. In that year Arthur Fiedler began a fifty-year reign, as the first American-born conductor. He regretted that classical music seemed to be mainly for wealthy concertgoers and took it to a broader audience, including through free concerts at the Hatch Shell along the Charles River. He had the orchestra play both popular music and well-known classics, and so created a new niche for popular symphonic music. The best-known pieces for the orchestra were the colourful novelties of Fiedler's friend Leroy Anderson, such as Sleigh Ride, The Typewriter and The Syncopated Clock. Fiedler also started the annual Holiday Pops in December. In July 1935 the orchestra made its first recordings for RCA Victor, with the first complete recording of George Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue.

Today the orchestra gives a popular music season in the spring and a Christmas programme in December, under the direction of Keith Lockhart. Every year on 4 July it plays at the Hatch Shell, with Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture and Sousa's The Stars and Stripes Forever. The Boston Pops showed that a symphony orchestra can also reach an audience that listens to pop music.
artiest/boston-pops-orchestra.listen: Listen to Leroy Anderson's Sleigh Ride in a recording by the Boston Pops and notice the whip crack and the hoofbeats. Hear how a symphony orchestra uses them to turn a tune into a picture.

artiest/boston-symphony-orchestra.text:
The Boston Symphony Orchestra is an American orchestra from Boston and the second-oldest orchestra in the United States. It is one of the five great American orchestras known as the Big Five. Henry Lee Higginson founded it in 1881, and the first concert was given on 22 October 1881, with works by Beethoven, Haydn, Gluck, Schubert and Weber. The first conductor was George Henschel, a well-known baritone and a good friend of Johannes Brahms. He sent Brahms his new seating plans for the orchestra and received a letter of approval in return. The orchestra plays most of its concerts in Symphony Hall in Boston, and in the summer at Tanglewood.

The first music directors were all trained in Austria, as Higginson wanted, among them Arthur Nikisch. Later the orchestra was led by Serge Koussevitzky, Pierre Monteux, Charles Munch, Erich Leinsdorf, William Steinberg and James Levine. It has had seventeen music directors in all, and Andris Nelsons is the current one. Bernard Haitink was principal guest conductor from 1995 to 2004 and then conductor emeritus until his death in 2021. The orchestra has been making gramophone recordings since 1917, including The Rite of Spring in 1951 and Symphonie fantastique in 1955, and has sometimes played on film soundtracks, such as that of Schindler's List.

The Boston Pops, also founded by Higginson in 1885 for concerts of a lighter kind of music, consists largely of musicians from this orchestra and has its own programme and conductor. In this way the Boston Symphony Orchestra stands for the classical tradition in America, with a line of European conductors who shaped its sound.
artiest/boston-symphony-orchestra.listen: Listen to the opening of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring in the 1951 recording and notice the bassoon playing at the very top of its range. Hear how the orchestra grows from there into a hard, rhythmic sound.

artiest/bots.text:
Bots is a Dutch-language folk rock band from Eindhoven, formed in 1974. The singer Hans Sanders was then studying at the Sociale Academie (a college of social work) and started the group with, among others, Bonkie Bongaerts. The name comes from the Dutch verb botsen, to collide. The band came from left-wing circles and called its own music strijdcultuur, a culture of struggle: the lyrics dealt with young workers, feminism, racism, solidarity and militarism. Peter Koelewijn produced the first albums, beginning with Van kwaad tot erger in 1975.

The best-known record is Zeven dagen lang from the 1976 album Voor God en vaderland. It is an adaptation of the Breton folk song Son ar Chistr, which Alan Stivell had made famous. In the music you hear folk and pop intermingled, with flute and saxophone alongside guitars and piano. In Germany Bots became even more popular than at home, in both the West and the GDR, where the band was already touring in 1977. From 1980 the group also sang in German. Aufstehn included Sieben Tage lang, and Entrüstung from 1981 included Das weiche Wasser, a protest song against the deployment of cruise missiles.

In this way Bots became a voice of the peace movement of the early 1980s. In 1983 the band played in West Berlin, for free, to an enormous audience at the festival Künstler für den Frieden. Disputes over money and changes in the line-up followed. Sanders died in 2007, but Zeven dagen lang remained well known, including through a new version with Ali B from 2005.
artiest/bots.listen: Listen to Zeven dagen lang. Notice the melody that circles like a folk dance and the chorus that the whole group sings together: a song to sing along to with a packed hall.

artiest/boudewijn-de-groot.text:
Boudewijn de Groot was born on 20 May 1944 in Tjideng, a Japanese internment camp in Batavia, present-day Jakarta. His mother died in the same camp in 1945. After the war he grew up in Haarlem and Heemstede. There he met Lennaert Nijgh, who became his regular lyricist. Together they brought the Dutch-language song closer to pop in the 1960s.

His first recordings from 1964 made no impact. The turning point came in 1966 with the producer Tony Vos. Welterusten mijnheer de president, with lyrics by Nijgh and music by De Groot, was released in April 1966 and reached number 9 in the Top 40. It is a protest song against the Vietnam War, addressed to the American president Lyndon Johnson. It is on his self-titled debut album from that year. Later in 1966 came Voor de overlevenden. It includes Het land van Maas en Waal, which reached number 1 as a single in 1967. Picknick (1968) showed the influence of Sgt. Pepper by The Beatles.

De Groot did not like to see himself as a protest singer, but the song kept circulating. De Heideroosjes and De Dijk made their own versions of it. Avond, a single from 1997, was at number 1 in the Top 2000 of NPO Radio 2 in 2005. His line of personal, singable songs in his own language runs on to Acda en de Munnik and, with the protest song, to Froukje.
artiest/boudewijn-de-groot.listen: In Welterusten mijnheer de president, listen for the contrast: the melody rocks like a lullaby, while the lyrics confront the president with the dead in Vietnam. The song never rose higher than number 9 in the Top 40, but in 2007 and 2010 it topped a Top 100 of protest songs.

artiest/bournemouth-symphony-orchestra.text:
The Bournemouth Symphony Orchestra is an English orchestra, founded in Bournemouth in 1893. Since 1979 its administration has been in neighbouring Poole, where the orchestra is based at the Lighthouse. It also plays in Portsmouth, Exeter and Bristol and is meant to serve the south and south-west of England. Dan Godfrey founded it as the Bournemouth Municipal Orchestra, a group of thirty wind players and a drummer. Many musicians could play both wind and string instruments, so that the group could play as a military band on the pier and as a classical ensemble indoors. The first concert was on Whit Monday 1893 in the Winter Gardens.

The orchestra quickly became a full symphony orchestra and gained a reputation as a champion of British music. Edward Elgar and Gustav Holst conducted their own works there, and it gave the British premières of major works by Richard Strauss, Camille Saint-Saëns and Tchaikovsky. In 1903 it gave its five-hundredth symphony concert, and in 1927 its Easter festival was devoted to music by British women composers. Godfrey, still the longest-serving chief conductor, conducted more than two thousand symphony concerts and retired in 1934. The orchestra's first recording dates from 1914. Later came recordings such as Scheherazade in 1967 and The Planets in 1974.

Later chief conductors included Rudolf Schwarz, Constantin Silvestri, Paavo Berglund, Andrew Litton, Marin Alsop and Kirill Karabits. Since the 2024–25 season it has been Mark Wigglesworth. The orchestra shows that a seasonal orchestra in a seaside town could grow into an ensemble of national importance, with a special place for British composers.
artiest/bournemouth-symphony-orchestra.listen: Listen to Gustav Holst's The Planets in the 1974 recording and notice Mars, with its five-beat rhythm. Observe how the orchestra builds a menacing sound out of it.

artiest/bow-wow-wow.text:
Bow Wow Wow was an English new wave band put together by the manager Malcolm McLaren in 1980. McLaren, the former manager of the Sex Pistols, lured guitarist Matthew Ashman, bassist Leigh Gorman and drummer David Barbarossa away from Adam and the Ants. After a search of six months, a talent scout found the thirteen-year-old Annabella Lwin, who was singing along to the radio in a dry cleaner's in West Hampstead. For a short time George Alan O'Dowd was also a second singer; he soon afterwards founded Culture Club and became famous as Boy George.

In July 1980 the band signed to EMI. Its first single, C30 C60 C90 Go!, was released at first on cassette only and was the world's first cassette single. The lyrics encouraged home taping from the radio, at a time when music piracy was a sensitive subject, and EMI therefore did not promote the record. It nevertheless reached number 34 in the British chart. In November came the cassette mini-album Your Cassette Pet. Both were counted by NME among the best tracks of 1980. When the second single did not chart, EMI dropped the group. After that came See Jungle! See Jungle! Go Join Your Gang Yeah! City All Over, Go Ape Crazy in 1981 and When the Going Gets Tough the Tough Get Going in 1983. In 1982 the band had its first British top ten hit with Go Wild in the Country.

The sound was danceable new wave on a Burundi beat, played by Barbarossa on drums, with exuberant, provocative lyrics that the teenage singer sang and shouted. Bow Wow Wow showed that African rhythms and punk style could come together in a pop band, led by a manager who used provocation as advertising.
artiest/bow-wow-wow.listen: Listen to C30 C60 C90 Go! and notice the drum patterns beneath the vocals. Hear how the beat resembles African drums more than ordinary rock drumming.

artiest/boy-george.text:
Boy George's real name is George Alan O'Dowd. He was born in 1961 and grew up in Eltham, in south-east London, in an Irish Catholic working-class family. School did not go well and he left without qualifications. He lived in squats and belonged to the New Romantics who went out at the club Blitz. His role models were Siouxsie Sioux, Roxy Music, David Bowie and Marc Bolan. Malcolm McLaren briefly had him perform with Bow Wow Wow, under the name Lieutenant Lush.

In 1981 he formed the band Culture Club with bassist Mikey Craig, drummer Jon Moss and guitarist Roy Hay. The debut album Kissing to Be Clever came out in 1982 and the single Do You Really Want to Hurt Me became an international hit. Time (Clock of the Heart), Church of the Poison Mind and Karma Chameleon followed, the last from the 1983 album Colour by Numbers. The music mixed pop, new wave, soul and reggae, and above it sounded his soft, soulful voice.

From 1987 he worked solo and had hits with Everything I Own and The Crying Game. With the group Jesus Loves You he had hits such as Generations of Love around 1990, and later he also became a DJ. As important as the music was his appearance. With make-up, hats and an androgynous style he showed that a pop star did not have to fit into a box. He was openly gay, at a time when that was anything but a matter of course for a teen idol.
artiest/boy-george.listen: Listen to Do You Really Want to Hurt Me by Culture Club. Notice the calm, swaying rhythm and the soft, soulful way Boy George sings: not a scream, but a lament.

artiest/brad-mehldau.text: The pianist Brad Mehldau grew up in Florida and Connecticut and studied in New York. He played with the saxophonist Joshua Redman and in 1995 started a trio of his own. He was often compared with Bill Evans and Keith Jarrett, but developed a way of playing of his own in which both hands play independent melodies, as in the music of Bach. Besides standards, Mehldau also plays pop songs, from Radiohead and Nick Drake to the Beatles. In this way he reached an audience beyond jazz. He has also written for classical singers and worked with the mandolin player Chris Thile.
artiest/brad-mehldau.listen: Follow the two hands: each plays a melody of its own.

artiest/brainpower.text:
Brainpower is the stage name of Gertjan Mulder, a Dutch-language rapper, born on 5 February 1975 in Antwerp and raised in Alphen aan den Rijn. He began rapping in the mid-1980s and returned in the 1990s to Amsterdam, his mother's city. His career began in 1998, when he took part in the Grote Prijs van Nederland, a talent contest for Dutch musicians. In 1999 he rapped on Zoete Inval by Extince, and in 2000 on Als niet Als by Doe Maar. In the same year his first single, Door Merg en Brain, was released, and in 2001 the debut album of the same name.

In 2002 came the album Verschil moet er zijn, with Dansplaat as its first single. It topped the charts in the Netherlands and Belgium. That year he also started the rap group ADHD and won an MTV Award for best Dutch act. In 2003 a live album appeared, followed by an eighteen-month tour. Later came Even stil in 2005 and the double album Hart en Hard in 2008. In 2009 the box set Mijn Manier was released, with all thirty videos. In 2010 he played in Jamaica with the reggae and dancehall legend Yellowman and released Dub en Dwars, with re-recorded reggae versions of his biggest songs.

Brainpower became the best-selling Dutch-language solo rapper of all time. He showed that rap could work in Dutch, with wordplay and humour, and that a Dutch rapper could find his way to reggae and dancehall.
artiest/brainpower.listen: Listen to Dansplaat from 2002 and notice the wordplay in the lyrics. Try to hear how fast, and yet how clearly intelligible, he raps.

artiest/brand-new-heavies.text:
The Brand New Heavies is an English band formed in 1985 by Simon Bartholomew, Jan Kincaid and Andrew Levy, at first under the name Brother International. A demo went down well in a London club, and in 1987 they opened for James Brown at Wembley Arena. Shortly afterwards they chose their new name, inspired by a nickname of Brown's, Minister of New Super Heavy Funk. In 1988 the single Got to Give was released, and in 1989 they moved to Eddie Piller's Acid Jazz Records, where they helped to shape a new genre: acid jazz.

Their debut album was released in 1990. A reissue in 1991 had new vocals by the American N'Dea Davenport, who had joined the group. The singles Never Stop, Dream Come True and Don't Let It Go to Your Head were a success. The breakthrough album was Brother Sister from 1994, with Dream On Dreamer. Later Davenport left, Siedah Garrett came in for the album Shelter in 1997, and Davenport returned in 2006 for Get Used to It.

Acid jazz mixes jazz, funk and soul with dance rhythms. The band plays real instruments, with a tight rhythm section and a female singer up front. It is regarded as one of the most important groups of the genre and shows how James Brown's funk found new life in London.
artiest/brand-new-heavies.listen: Listen to Never Stop. Notice the walking bass line and the brass section, and how the vocals float lightly and smoothly on top.

artiest/branford-marsalis.text: The saxophonist Branford Marsalis, Wynton's older brother, played with Art Blakey and in his brother's quintet in the early 1980s. Sonny Rollins and John Coltrane were his most important models. He also played with Sting and from 1992 to 1995 led the band of The Tonight Show. With his project Buckshot LeFonque he mixed jazz with hip-hop. His quartet has been playing acoustic jazz for decades, and in 2002 recorded a version of A Love Supreme of its own. He also founded a label of his own, Marsalis Music.
artiest/branford-marsalis.listen: Listen to the tenor sax moving between tradition and a voice of its own.

artiest/bratmobile.text:
Bratmobile is an American punk band from Olympia, in the state of Washington, and one of the first riot grrrl bands. Allison Wolfe and Molly Neuman met in 1989 as neighbours in a student house in Oregon. Both came from activist families. Together they took women's studies classes, went to Olympia at weekends and made the feminist fanzine Girl Germs. The musician Calvin Johnson asked them on Valentine's Day 1991 to perform alongside Bikini Kill. They did not yet play any instruments, but they did have songs. A musician advised them to listen to the Ramones. Wolfe did exactly the opposite, so that they would sound different from the boys' bands.

Soon afterwards the guitarist Erin Smith joined and the band became a trio: Wolfe sang, Neuman drummed and Smith played guitar. In 1991 they played at the International Pop Underground Convention in Olympia, an important moment for the movement. Their music is bare and direct, with influences from pop, surf music and garage rock: short songs, simple guitar, solid drums and mocking, defiant vocals. In 1993 the album Pottymouth was released on the label Kill Rock Stars.

The media attention around riot grrrl put the band under pressure. In 1994 Bratmobile fell apart on stage during a chaotic performance in New York. In 1999 they got together again and went on to make Ladies, Women and Girls (2000) and Girls Get Busy (2002). Like Bikini Kill, Bratmobile showed that girls in punk could claim a place of their own.
artiest/bratmobile.listen: Listen to Cherry Bomb by Bratmobile from 1993. Notice how simple and raw the guitar and drums sound, and the brash, half-shouted singing of Allison Wolfe.

artiest/bread.text:
Bread was an American soft rock band from Los Angeles, California. Its frontman was David Gates from Tulsa, Oklahoma, who sang and played bass, guitar, keyboards and violin. Beside him were Jimmy Griffin on vocals and guitar and Robb Royer on bass, guitar and flute. Gates had produced Royer's earlier band, the Pleasure Fair. Royer introduced him to his writing partner Griffin, and in 1968 the trio formed a group that signed to Elektra in January 1969. The name came from a bread van that drove past while they were looking for a name. It began with a B, like The Beatles and The Bee Gees.

The debut album Bread was released in September 1969, with the songs divided equally between Gates and the duo of Griffin and Royer. Drummer Mike Botts became a permanent member in the summer of 1969. With On the Waters in 1970 Bread became a major group, thanks to Make It with You, their only number one on the Billboard Hot 100, in 1970. It Don't Matter to Me followed, then the third album Manna in 1971 with If and Let Your Love Go, and Baby I'm-A Want You and Guitar Man in 1972. In 1971 Royer left the band, after which Larry Knechtel took his place on keyboards, bass, guitar and harmonica. Between 1970 and 1977 thirteen songs reached the Hot 100, and in 1977 Lost Without Your Love was released.

Bread made soft, melodic pop songs with acoustic guitars and warm vocals. They show that in the 1970s, alongside hard rock and glam rock, a quiet, loving pop style could be big.
artiest/bread.listen: Listen to Make It with You from 1970 and notice the soft guitar and David Gates's calm voice. Try to hear how few instruments the song needs.

artiest/brecon-baroque.text:
Brecon Baroque is an ensemble that plays Baroque music, named after the Welsh town of Brecon in Powys. It plays mainly the repertoire of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and has been releasing albums since 2010.

The series begins with Violin Concertos in 2010, followed by Double & Triple Concertos in 2013. After that the musicians chose works that every Baroque lover knows: L'estro armonico in 2015, The Art of Fugue in 2016 and Le Quattro Stagioni in 2018. In between comes Grandissima Gravita in 2017. More recently came Goldberg Variations Reimagined in 2023, The Muses Restor'd in 2024 and Just Biber in 2025. So the line runs from Vivaldi and Bach to the violinist and composer Biber.

The ensemble belongs to the movement that plays early music in the ways the composers themselves knew. This produces a clear, transparent sound in which every voice remains easy to follow. For anyone who knows pop, this is the world that harmony, bass lines and repeated patterns come from, which later return in every genre.
artiest/brecon-baroque.listen: Listen to Le Quattro Stagioni and notice how the soloist and the string orchestra take turns. Try to hear where the orchestra plays a recurring theme and where the soloist plays freely over it.

artiest/brennan-heart.text:
Brennan Heart is the pseudonym of Fabian Bohn, a Dutch hardstyle DJ and producer, born in 1982 in Helden. In 2002 he began making music on the border of hardcore and hard trance, which developed into hardstyle. He did so at first as the duo Brennan & Heart with Pieter Heijnen, who later continued as DJ Thera. When the duo split after a little over three years, Bohn kept the name Brennan Heart.

In 2006 he joined the label Scantraxx Records and under it set up his own sublabel M!D!FY. His first solo album, Musical Impressions, was released in 2009. Evolution of Style followed in 2014, I Am Hardstyle in 2016, ON DEMAND in 2017, Show Your True Colors in 2019 and Brennan Heart And Friends in 2020. In 2012 he started his own label, later called WE R Music, and in 2015 he launched the brand I AM HARDSTYLE at the Amsterdam Dance Event. He has performed at festivals such as Defqon.1 and Qlimax.

Hardstyle is built on hard, distorted bass drums, high synthesizer melodies and an arc of tension from build-up to release. Brennan Heart became one of the faces of that scene in the Netherlands, which he also shaped as a label boss and event organiser.
artiest/brennan-heart.listen: Listen to a track from Evolution of Style, for example Lose My Mind. Notice the bass drum that keeps returning, the build-up to the drop and the melody that then carries the track.

artiest/brennan-heart-en-jonathan-mendel.text:
Brennan Heart is a hardstyle producer. Jonathan Mendelsohn is an American singer and songwriter, born in 1980 in Brooklyn and raised in upstate New York. He began writing songs at the age of ten, after his mother, a teacher and pianist, had taught him chord changes. He cites Top 40 radio and singers such as Mariah Carey, Whitney Houston and George Michael as influences, and came to know electronic music in the New York rave scene of the late 1990s. In 2002 he won a talent contest at the Apollo Theater.

In dance music he worked with DJs such as Hardwell, Blasterjaxx and Laidback Luke. In 2013 he sang Imaginary for Brennan Heart. The track was part of the closing show of Defqon.1 and appeared on Brennan's album Evolution of Style. It topped Beatport's Hard Dance chart and stayed in the top hundred for 777 days. Q-dance chose it as the best hardstyle track of the year. In the Netherlands Imaginary went gold in 2019 and platinum in 2022.

Hardstyle is hard dance music with a heavy, distorted kick drum and a rhythm that keeps the dance floor moving. Imaginary shows how the style reached a large audience with a real singer and a melodic chorus. For Mendelsohn it was one of the collaborations that made his name known in dance.
artiest/brennan-heart-en-jonathan-mendel.listen: Listen to Imaginary. Notice the contrast between Mendelsohn's calm, melodic vocals and the hard kick drum that comes in afterwards.

artiest/brian-eno.text:
Brian Eno is an English musician, producer and artist, born in 1948 in Melton, Suffolk. He studied at art schools in Ipswich and Winchester and calls himself a non-musician: virtuosity does not interest him. Even at school he used a tape recorder as an instrument. In 1971 he joined the glam rock band Roxy Music, where he operated the synthesizer and tape effects on the first two albums. In 1973 he left after a disagreement with Bryan Ferry.

His first solo records, Here Come the Warm Jets and Taking Tiger Mountain (by Strategy), still contained songs. On Another Green World, from 1975, he already combined rock with quiet, instrumental pieces. After that he devised the term ambient: music that you can also ignore. Ambient 1: Music for Airports became the best-known example. Eno uses the studio itself as an instrument to compose with, and he likes to let chance play a part.

As a producer he left his mark on rock music. With David Bowie he made the albums Low, Heroes and Lodger, together the Berlin Trilogy. He produced Talking Heads, including Remain in Light, and together with Daniel Lanois the great U2 records The Unforgettable Fire, The Joshua Tree and Achtung Baby. Later came Coldplay's Viva la Vida. In the course he appears in the story about electronic music, as someone who sensed early on which way the sound of the future was heading. Many ambient makers regard him as the founder of the genre.
artiest/brian-eno.listen: Listen to Ambient 1: Music for Airports. Notice how little happens: a few calm notes keep coming back, without a beat and without a chorus, so that the music can hang in the space as background.

artiest/brian-holland.text:
Brian Holland is an American songwriter and producer, born in 1941 in Detroit. His older brother Eddie Holland became his regular partner. Brian himself also appeared on stage: in 1958 he released a first single, and around 1960 he sang with the Satintones and in the Rayber Voices, a vocal group that backed early Motown records. Together with Robert Bateman he wrote Please Mr. Postman for the Marvelettes under the name Brianbert. That 1961 record became Motown's first number 1 hit and was later covered by The Beatles.

He then formed the trio Holland-Dozier-Holland with Lamont Dozier and his brother Eddie. In it Brian was mainly the arranger and producer. The team wrote hits such as Stop! In the Name of Love and Back in My Arms Again for The Supremes, (Love Is Like a) Heatwave and Jimmy Mack for Martha and the Vandellas, and Reach Out, I'll Be There and Bernadette for the Four Tops. The Isley Brothers and Jr. Walker and the All Stars also recorded their songs.

The songs of Holland-Dozier-Holland largely determined how the Motown sound sounded: catchy melodies, a solid beat and full accompaniment. In 1967 the trio left Motown after a dispute over their contract. In the 1970s Brian again made records of his own, with smaller hits on the R&B chart. In 2019 he wrote the autobiography Come and Get These Memories with Eddie and Dave Thompson, named after a hit by Martha and the Vandellas.
artiest/brian-holland.listen: Listen to Stop! In the Name of Love by The Supremes. Notice how the accompaniment grows fuller towards the chorus, and how the chorus, with the single phrase of its title, sticks in your head at once.

artiest/brian-johnson.text:
Brian Johnson is an English singer, born in 1947 in Dunston near Newcastle. His father was a miner and a soldier; his mother came from Frascati in Italy. He started in small bands and from 1970 played in a cabaret and club band, from which the rock band Geordie emerged in Newcastle in 1971. With them he had hit singles in the early 1970s, including All Because of You in 1973. In 1978 Geordie broke up.

The turning point came in 1980. After the death of Bon Scott on 19 February, the brothers Angus and Malcolm Young looked for a new singer for AC/DC. Scott had earlier heard Johnson sing in England and had praised him as a rock 'n' roller in the style of Little Richard. Johnson was allowed to audition in March, sang Nutbush City Limits among other songs, and got the job. His first album with the band, Back in Black, became one of the best-selling albums ever.

His voice is high, rasping and unmistakable, with a strong Geordie accent. In 2003 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with AC/DC. In 2016 he temporarily left the tour because of hearing problems, but he returned for the album Power Up. Johnson shows that a band can carry on after a loss without losing its sound.
artiest/brian-johnson.listen: Listen to Back in Black and notice Johnson's voice. Hear how he keeps rising above the heavy, tight guitar riff, rasping and almost screaming.

artiest/brian-jones.text:
Brian Jones was an English musician and the founder of The Rolling Stones. He was born in 1942 in Cheltenham and was a great lover of American blues. In 1962 he brought together in London the band in which Mick Jagger and Keith Richards also played. In the first years he was the musical driving force of the group, with slide guitar and harmonica.

Jones could quickly learn to play almost any instrument he came across. This gave the Stones' music new colours in the 1960s: the sitar in Paint It Black, the marimba in Under My Thumb and the recorder in Ruby Tuesday. On the 1967 album Their Satanic Majesties Request he played the Mellotron, a keyboard instrument that plays back recorded sounds of strings and wind instruments. In this way he helped the band to a richer, layered sound in the psychedelic years.

As Jagger and Richards increasingly wrote the songs, Jones slipped into the background. His drug use made working together harder, and in June 1969 he left the band. A month later, on 3 July 1969, he was found dead in the swimming pool at his home. He was 27. His role as founder, and as the man who gave the Stones so many tone colours, is still mentioned whenever he comes up.
artiest/brian-jones.listen: Listen to She's a Rainbow by The Rolling Stones. Notice Brian Jones's Mellotron alongside the piano and the strings: it provides the soft, fairy-tale sound beneath the vocals.

artiest/brian-poole-and-the-tremeloes.text:
Brian Poole and the Tremeloes was an English beat group from Dagenham, formed in 1958. The singer Brian Poole played with lead guitarist Rick Westwood, rhythm guitarist Alan Blakley, bassist Alan Howard and drummer Dave Munden. The band was strongly influenced by Buddy Holly and the Crickets.

On New Year's Day 1962 the record company Decca held an audition for two young groups: the Tremeloes and The Beatles from Liverpool. Decca chose the Tremeloes, reportedly partly because they came from near London and so were easier to reach. In 1963 they entered the British chart with a version of Twist and Shout, which The Beatles had put on their first album shortly before. That same year came Do You Love Me, a cover of an American hit, which reached number 1. Candy Man and Someone, Someone also became hits. They were cheerful, simple beat versions of existing songs.

In 1966 Poole left and the group continued as The Tremeloes. All the members sang, and with harmonies and a more contemporary sound they scored again: Here Comes My Baby and Silence Is Golden from 1967, the second number 1, and later (Call Me) Number One. Yet the group remains known above all as the band that beat The Beatles at Decca, a choice the company soon regretted.
artiest/brian-poole-and-the-tremeloes.listen: Listen to Do You Love Me by Brian Poole and the Tremeloes. Notice the energetic beat accompaniment with guitars and drums and the singer who is constantly answered by the band.

artiest/brian-reitzell.text:
Brian Reitzell is an American musician, composer, producer and music supervisor, born in 1965. He began as the drummer of the Los Angeles punk band Redd Kross. Later he became best known for his work for film and television, in which he not only writes music but also chooses and brings together existing songs.

His name is closely linked with the director Sofia Coppola, for whom he worked on The Virgin Suicides, Lost in Translation, Marie Antoinette and The Bling Ring. For the score of Lost in Translation he received a BAFTA nomination in 2003 together with Kevin Shields of My Bloody Valentine. He also collaborated often with the French duo Air: he played drums on The Virgin Suicides and 10 000 Hz Legend and toured with them in 1998, 2000 and 2001. He also made music for 30 Days of Night in 2007, the television series Boss, Hannibal and American Gods and the games Red Faction: Armageddon and Watch Dogs. In 2014 his first solo album, Auto Music, was released.

Reitzell shows how atmosphere in visual media can be built from layers of guitar, electronics and sound, often close to pop music. He is one of the makers who tie pop taste and film music together.
artiest/brian-reitzell.listen: Listen to an excerpt from the Hannibal soundtrack and notice how the music creates more atmosphere and tension than melody. Try to hear which sounds you do not immediately recognise as an instrument.

artiest/brian-wilson.text:
Brian Wilson (1942 to 2025) was an American musician, singer, songwriter and producer and the founder of the Beach Boys. In 1961 he began his professional career with the band. He wrote, produced, sang, played bass and keyboards and was in effect the leader. After signing to Capitol Records in 1962 he became the first pop musician to be recognised for writing, arranging, producing and performing his own material. He also made records for others, such as the Honeys, Jan & Dean and Glen Campbell.

By the mid-1960s he had already written or co-written two dozen American top 40 hits, including the number 1 hits Surf City in 1963, I Get Around in 1964, Help Me, Rhonda in 1965 and Good Vibrations in 1966. His models included George Gershwin, the Four Freshmen, Phil Spector and Burt Bacharach. His work stands out for its rich harmonies, orchestrations and vocal arrangements, and for his head voice and falsetto. He struggled with mental health problems all his life. Those problems also shaped his career.

As a solo artist he released, among others, Brian Wilson in 1988, SMiLE in 2004, That Lucky Old Sun in 2008 and No Pier Pressure in 2015. Wilson is regarded as the first rock producer to use the studio as an instrument, and so as one of the most important innovators in pop history.
artiest/brian-wilson.listen: Listen to Good Vibrations and notice how the song consists of several sections, each with its own mood. Hear how vocals, bass and strings are layered differently each time.

artiest/bridges.text:
Bridges was a Norwegian rock band from Oslo, formed in 1978. Pål Waaktaar and Magne Furuholmen both grew up in Manglerud, a suburb of Oslo. Already in fifth grade Waaktaar, still a drummer at the time, brought Furuholmen into his little band as guitarist and singer. Later Waaktaar learned to play guitar himself and persuaded Furuholmen to take up keyboards. With bassist Viggo Bondi and drummer Erik Hagelien the group began recording demos.

In 1978 and 1979 Bridges played live a number of times. At one of those concerts Morten Harket was in the audience. For the debut album Fakkeltog, Øystein Jevanord took over on drums. The band paid for the recording and release itself, and the record came out in 1980. In the summer of 1981 a second album, Våkenatt, was finished, but the atmosphere in the group had worsened during the recording. After a last concert that summer the band broke up, without the album having been released.

Waaktaar and Furuholmen wanted to continue in London, but the other two did not go with them. With Morten Harket they then started the synth-pop group a-ha. That is why Bridges is important above all as a forerunner: this is where the later makers of a-ha learned to write and record songs together. Våkenatt was not released until 2018, by the Norwegian music archive Rockheim.
artiest/bridges.listen: Listen to a track from Fakkeltog and compare it with Take On Me by a-ha. Notice whether you can already hear something of the later synth-pop sound in Furuholmen's keyboards.

artiest/brij-bhushan-kabra.text:
Brij Bhushan Kabra (1937 to 2018) was an Indian musician who made the guitar known in Indian classical music. He was born in Jodhpur and studied to become a geologist. During a visit to Kolkata he discovered the Hawaiian lap steel guitar. He persuaded his father to let him learn to play by promising that he would play only classical music. He learned the instrument by copying records and later studied with Ali Akbar Khan. He adapted the guitar with sympathetic strings and drone strings.

Kabra was the first Indian musician to play ragas on the guitar. His album Call of the Valley, recorded with the flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia and the santoor player Shivkumar Sharma, was a success. Later came, among others, Exotic Sounds on Guitar, Indian Slide Guitar / Raga Puriya Alap and Jugalbandi, a duet for violin and guitar. In the 1990s he concentrated mainly on teaching, but he continued to perform. In 2005 he received the national Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

The sound is that of a guitar that sings: long, gliding notes above a continuous drone. In the 1970s this music found a large audience in hippie culture. In this way Kabra belongs among the Indian musicians who introduced Western pop musicians to raga and drone.
artiest/brij-bhushan-kabra.listen: Listen to Call of the Valley and follow the guitar. Hear how the tone glides instead of jumping from string to string, and how an unchanging foundation carries the melody.

artiest/britney-spears.text:
Britney Spears was born in 1981 in McComb, in the American state of Mississippi, and grew up in Kentwood, Louisiana. As a child she was already on television in The All-New Mickey Mouse Club. In the late 1990s she became the face of a new wave of teen pop, made in Stockholm and sold to the whole world.

In 1997 she signed to Jive Records. She recorded her first single, ...Baby One More Time, in May 1998 at Cheiron Studios in Stockholm. Max Martin wrote the song and produced it with Rami Yacoub. It had earlier been offered to the Backstreet Boys and TLC, who both turned it down. The single was released in September 1998, when Spears was sixteen, and reached number 1 in more than twenty countries, including America and England. The album of the same name (1999) sold more than ten million copies in the United States. Oops!... I Did It Again (2000) and In the Zone (2003) followed, the latter with Toxic, which won a Grammy.

Spears showed how Max Martin's hit factory worked: the music was largely ready, and the singer made the song her own. From 2008 her life was under a conservatorship held by her father. It was not until 2021 that this came to an end, after she herself had testified against her family and management. Her book The Woman in Me was published in 2023.
artiest/britney-spears.listen: ...Baby One More Time (1998) opens with three low piano notes and, straight afterwards, the voice: "Oh baby, baby". Notice how the hook lands in the very first seconds, with no intro to skip through.

artiest/bronski-beat.text:
Bronski Beat was a synth-pop group from London, formed in 1983. The singer Jimmy Somerville and keyboard player Steve Bronski came from Glasgow, keyboard player Larry Steinbachek from Essex. They shared a flat in Brixton. All three were openly gay, and they wanted to be more outspoken and more political than the gay artists of the time.

After fewer than ten performances the group signed to London Records in 1984. The first single, Smalltown Boy, is about a gay boy who flees his family and his town. It reached number 1 in the Netherlands and Belgium, among other countries. Then came Why?, with a fast Hi-NRG sound and lyrics about prejudice against gay people, and the album The Age of Consent. The inner sleeve listed the different ages of consent for gay sex in countries around the world. The music consisted of cool synthesizers and electronic beats, with Somerville's high falsetto above them.

In 1985 the group recorded a medley with Marc Almond built around Donna Summer's I Feel Love. That year Somerville left. He started The Communards, and with his successor John Foster Bronski Beat still scored with Hit That Perfect Beat. The band also supported the striking miners with a benefit concert. Bronski Beat was one of the British acts who came out openly about their sexuality in the 1980s, and showed that a pop song about the experience of gay teenagers could become a big hit.
artiest/bronski-beat.listen: Listen to Smalltown Boy. Notice the contrast between the cool, repeating synthesizers and the high, vulnerable voice of Jimmy Somerville, who tells the story of the boy who leaves.
